headline: Primary school headteacher dies after falling from rickshaw during mugging near parliament
summary: Ronjina Parvin, 55, suffered severe head injuries after two motorcycle-borne muggers tried to snatch her bag in Dhaka.
details: Ronjina Parvin, the 55-year-old headmistress of Bagbari Girls Government Primary School in Bogura, died this morning after a mugging attempt in Dhaka.
The incident occurred around 6:30 am near the South Plaza area of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban (Parliament) complex.
Ronjina had traveled from Bogura with her husband to visit the Ispahani Islamia Eye Institute and Hospital at Farmgate for a medical consultation.
According to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police, two muggers on a motorcycle approached from behind and tried to snatch her bag while she was in a rickshaw.
During the scuffle, Ronjina fell from the rickshaw and sustained severe head injuries.
She was rushed to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared her dead.
caption:
A primary school headteacher has died after falling from a rickshaw during a mugging attempt in front of the National Parliament.

Ronjina Parvin, the 55-year-old headmistress of Bagbari Girls Government Primary School in Bogura, died this morning after a mugging attempt in Dhaka.

The incident occurred around 6:30 am near the South Plaza area of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban (Parliament) complex.

Ronjina had traveled from Bogura with her husband to visit the Ispahani Islamia Eye Institute and Hospital at Farmgate for a medical consultation.

According to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police, two muggers on a motorcycle approached from behind and tried to snatch her bag while she was in a rickshaw.

During the scuffle, Ronjina fell from the rickshaw and sustained severe head injuries.

She was rushed to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared her dead.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: MP Hummam Kader Chowdhury: [[Draft law on enforced disappearances]] prevents agency self-investigation
headline: MP Hummam Kader Chowdhury: Draft law on enforced disappearances prevents agency self-investigation
summary: The MP clarified that the proposed law ensures that the agency or force accused in a disappearance case cannot investigate the matter themselves.
details: MP Hummam Kader Chowdhury of the Chattogram-7 constituency stated that there are attempts to spread confusion among the general public regarding the law on enforced disappearances.
caption:
No agency can investigate its own accused members under the proposed enforced disappearances law, says MP Hummam Kader Chowdhury.

MP Hummam Kader Chowdhury of the Chattogram-7 constituency stated that there are attempts to spread confusion among the general public regarding the law on enforced disappearances.
